وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿لِنَعْلَمَ أيُّ الحِزْبَيْنِ أحْصى لِما لَبِثُوا أمَدًا﴾ فِيهِ مَسائِلُ:

**المَسْألَةُ الأُولى:** قَوْلُهُ: ﴿ثُمَّ بَعَثْناهم لِنَعْلَمَ﴾. اللّامُ لامُ الغَرَضِ (lam al-gharad, the lam of purpose)، فَيَدُلُّ عَلى أنَّ أفْعالَ اللَّهِ مُعَلَّلَةٌ بِالأغْراضِ، وقَدْ سَبَقَ الكَلامُ فِيهِ.

**المَسْألَةُ الثّانِيَةُ:** ظاهِرُ اللَّفْظِ يَقْتَضِي أنَّهُ تَعالى إنَّما بَعَثَهم لِيَحْصُلَ لَهُ هَذا العِلْمُ، وعِنْدَ هَذا يُرْجَعُ إلى أنَّهُ تَعالى، هَلْ يَعْلَمُ الحَوادِثَ قَبْلَ وُقُوعِها أمْ لا؟ فَقالَ هِشامٌ: لا يَعْلَمُها إلّا عِنْدَ حُدُوثِها، واحْتَجَّ بِهَذِهِ الآيَةِ، والكَلامُ فِيهِ قَدْ سَبَقَ. ونَظائِرُ هَذِهِ الآيَةِ كَثِيرَةٌ في القُرْآنِ، مِنها ما سَبَقَ في هَذِهِ السُّورَةِ، ومِنها قَوْلُهُ في سُورَةِ البَقَرَةِ: ﴿إلّا لِنَعْلَمَ مَن يَتَّبِعُ الرَّسُولَ مِمَّنْ يَنْقَلِبُ عَلى عَقِبَيْهِ﴾ (البَقَرَةِ: ١٤٣)، وفي آلِ عِمْرانَ: ﴿ولَمّا يَعْلَمِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ جاهَدُوا مِنكُمْ﴾ (آلِ عِمْرانَ: ١٤٢)، وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿إنّا جَعَلْنا ما عَلى الأرْضِ زِينَةً لَها لِنَبْلُوَهُمْ﴾ (الكَهْفِ: ٧)، وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿ولَنَبْلُوَنَّكم حَتّى نَعْلَمَ المُجاهِدِينَ مِنكُمْ﴾ (مُحَمَّدٍ: ٣١).

**المَسْألَةُ الثّالِثَةُ:** (أيُّ) مَرْفُوعٌ بِالِابْتِداءِ (mubtada’, the subject)، و(أحْصى) خَبَرُهُ (khabar, the predicate)، وهَذِهِ الجُمْلَةُ بِمَجْمُوعِها مُتَعَلِّقُ العِلْمِ. فَلِهَذا السَّبَبِ لَمْ يَظْهَرْ عَمَلُ قَوْلِهِ: (لِنَعْلَمَ) في لَفْظَةِ (أيُّ)، بَلْ بَقِيَتْ عَلى ارْتِفاعِها. ونَظِيرُهُ قَوْلُهُ: اذْهَبْ فاعْلَمْ أيُّهم قامَ. قالَ تَعالى: ﴿سَلْهم أيُّهم بِذَلِكَ زَعِيمٌ﴾ (القَلَمِ: ٤٠)، وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿ثُمَّ لَنَنْزِعَنَّ مِن كُلِّ شِيعَةٍ أيُّهم أشَدُّ عَلى الرَّحْمَنِ عِتِيًّا﴾ (مَرْيَمَ: ٦٩). وقُرِئَ «لِيُعْلَمَ» عَلى فِعْلِ ما لَمْ يُسَمَّ فاعِلُهُ، وفي هَذِهِ القِراءَةِ فائِدَتانِ:
إحْداهُما: أنَّ عَلى هَذا التَّقْدِيرِ لا يَلْزَمُ إثْباتُ العِلْمِ المُتَجَدِّدِ لِلَّهِ، بَلِ المَقْصُودُ أنّا بَعَثْناهم لِيَحْصُلَ هَذا العِلْمُ لِبَعْضِ الخَلْقِ.
والثّانِيَةُ: أنَّ عَلى هَذا التَّقْدِيرِ يَجِبُ ظُهُورُ النَّصْبِ في لَفْظَةِ (أيْ)، لَكِنْ لِقائِلٍ أنْ يَقُولَ: الإشْكالُ بَعْدُ باقٍ، لِأنَّ ارْتِفاعَ لَفْظَةِ (أيُّ) بِالِابْتِداءِ لا بِإسْنادٍ يُعْلَمُ إلَيْهِ. ولِمُجِيبٍ أنْ يُجِيبَ فَيَقُولَ: إنَّهُ لا يَمْتَنِعُ اجْتِماعُ عامِلَيْنِ عَلى مَعْمُولٍ واحِدٍ، لِأنَّ العَوامِلَ النَّحْوِيَّةَ عَلاماتٌ ومُعَرِّفاتٌ، ولا يَمْتَنِعُ اجْتِماعُ المُعَرِّفاتِ الكَثِيرَةِ عَلى الشَّيْءِ الواحِدِ. واللَّهُ أعْلَمُ.

**المَسْألَةُ الرّابِعَةُ:** اخْتَلَفُوا في الحِزْبَيْنِ. فَقالَ عَطاءٌ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُما: المُرادُ بِالحِزْبَيْنِ المُلُوكُ الَّذِينَ تَداوَلُوا المَدِينَةَ مَلِكًا بَعْدَ مَلِكٍ، فالمُلُوكُ حِزْبٌ وأصْحابُ الكَهْفِ حِزْبٌ.
والقَوْلُ الثّانِي: قالَ مُجاهِدٌ: الحِزْبانِ مِن هَذِهِ الفِتْيَةِ؛ لِأنَّ أصْحابَ الكَهْفِ لَمّا انْتَبَهُوا اخْتَلَفُوا في أنَّهم كَمْ نامُوا، والدَّلِيلُ عَلَيْهِ قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿قالَ قائِلٌ مِنهم كَمْ لَبِثْتُمْ قالُوا لَبِثْنا يَوْمًا أوْ بَعْضَ يَوْمٍ قالُوا رَبُّكم أعْلَمُ بِما لَبِثْتُمْ﴾ (الكَهْفِ: ١٩). فالحِزْبانِ هُما هَذانِ، وكانَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا: ﴿رَبُّكم أعْلَمُ بِما لَبِثْتُمْ﴾ هُمُ الَّذِينَ عَلِمُوا أنَّ لُبْثَهم قَدْ تَطاوَلَ.
القَوْلُ الثّالِثُ: قالَ الفَرّاءُ: إنَّ طائِفَتَيْنِ مِنَ المُسْلِمِينَ في زَمانِ أصْحابِ الكَهْفِ اخْتَلَفُوا في مُدَّةِ لُبْثِهِمْ.

**المَسْألَةُ الخامِسَةُ:** قالَ أبُو عَلِيٍّ الفارِسِيُّ: قَوْلُهُ (أحْصى) لَيْسَ مِن بابِ أفْعَلِ التَّفْضِيلِ (the comparative/superlative form)، لِأنَّ هَذا البِناءَ مِن غَيْرِ الثُّلاثِيِّ المُجَرَّدِ (the bare triliteral root) لَيْسَ بِقِياسٍ. فَأمّا قَوْلُهم: ما أعْطاهُ لِلدِّرْهَمِ، وما أوْلاهُ لِلْمَعْرُوفِ، وأعْدى مِنَ الجَرَبِ، وأفْلَسُ مِنَ ابْنِ المُدْلِقِ، فَمِنَ الشَّواذِّ، والشّاذُّ لا يُقاسُ عَلَيْهِ. بَلِ الصَّوابُ: أنَّ «أحْصى» فِعْلٌ ماضٍ، وهو خَبَرُ المُبْتَدَأِ، والمُبْتَدَأُ
صفحة ٧٢
والخَبَرُ مَفْعُولُ «نَعْلَمُ»، و«أمَدًا» مَفْعُولٌ بِهِ لِـ«أحْصى»، و«ما» في قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿لِما لَبِثُوا﴾ مَصْدَرِيَّةٌ، والتَّقْدِيرُ: أحْصى أمَدًا لِلُبْثِهِمْ. وحاصِلُ الكَلامِ: لِنَعْلَمَ أيُّ الحِزْبَيْنِ أحْصى أمَدَ ذَلِكَ اللُّبْثِ. ونَظِيرُهُ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿أحْصاهُ اللَّهُ﴾ (المُجادَلَةِ: ٦)، وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿وأحْصى كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عَدَدًا﴾ (الجِنِّ: ٢٨).

* * *

**المَسْألَةُ السّادِسَةُ:** احْتَجَّ أصْحابُنا الصُّوفِيَّةُ (the Sufis) بِهَذِهِ الآيَةِ عَلى صِحَّةِ القَوْلِ بِالكَراماتِ (karamat, divinely granted marvels of saints), وهو اسْتِدْلالٌ ظاهِرٌ. ونَذْكُرُ هَذِهِ المَسْألَةَ هَهُنا عَلى سَبِيلِ الِاسْتِقْصاءِ، فَنَقُولُ قَبْلَ الخَوْضِ في الدَّلِيلِ عَلى جَوازِ الكَراماتِ: نَفْتَقِرُ إلى تَقْدِيمِ مُقَدِّمَتَيْنِ:

**المُقَدِّمَةُ الأُولى:** في بَيانِ أنَّ الوَلِيَّ ما هُوَ. فَنَقُولُ: هَهُنا وَجْهانِ:
الأوَّلُ: أنْ يَكُونَ فَعِيلًا مُبالَغَةً مِنَ الفاعِلِ كَالعَلِيمِ والقَدِيرِ، فَيَكُونُ مَعْناهُ: مَن تَوالَتْ طاعاتُهُ مِن غَيْرِ تَخَلُّلِ مَعْصِيَةٍ.
الثّانِي: أنْ يَكُونَ فَعِيلًا بِمَعْنى مَفْعُولٍ كَقَتِيلٍ وجَرِيحٍ بِمَعْنى مَقْتُولٍ ومَجْرُوحٍ، وهُوَ الَّذِي يَتَوَلّى الحَقُّ سُبْحانَهُ حِفْظَهُ وحِراسَتَهُ عَلى التَّوالِي عَنْ كُلِّ أنْواعِ المَعاصِي، ويُدِيمُ تَوْفِيقَهُ عَلى الطّاعاتِ.
واعْلَمْ أنَّ هَذا الِاسْمَ مَأْخُوذٌ مِن قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿اللَّهُ ولِيُّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ (البَقَرَةِ: ٢٥٧)، وقَوْلِهِ: ﴿وهُوَ يَتَوَلّى الصّالِحِينَ﴾ (الأعْرافِ: ١٩٦)، وقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿أنْتَ مَوْلانا فانْصُرْنا عَلى القَوْمِ الكافِرِينَ﴾ (البَقَرَةِ: ٢٨٦)، وقَوْلِهِ: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأنَّ اللَّهَ مَوْلَى الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وأنَّ الكافِرِينَ لا مَوْلى لَهُمْ﴾ (مُحَمَّدٍ: ١١)، وقَوْلِهِ: ﴿إنَّما ولِيُّكُمُ اللَّهُ ورَسُولُهُ﴾ (المائِدَةِ: ٥٥). وأقُولُ: الوَلِيُّ هُوَ القَرِيبُ في اللُّغَةِ، فَإذا كانَ العَبْدُ قَرِيبًا مِن حَضْرَةِ اللَّهِ بِسَبَبِ كَثْرَةِ طاعاتِهِ وكَثْرَةِ إخْلاصِهِ، وكانَ الرَّبُّ قَرِيبًا مِنهُ بِرَحْمَتِهِ وفَضْلِهِ وإحْسانِهِ، فَهُناكَ حَصَلَتِ الوِلايَةُ.

**المُقَدِّمَةُ الثّانِيَةُ:** إذا ظَهَرَ فِعْلٌ خارِقٌ لِلْعادَةِ عَلى الإنْسانِ، فَذاكَ إمّا أنْ يَكُونَ مَقْرُونًا بِالدَّعْوى أوْ لا مَعَ الدَّعْوى. والقِسْمُ الأوَّلُ، وهو أنْ يَكُونَ مَعَ الدَّعْوى، فَتِلْكَ الدَّعْوى إمّا أنْ تَكُونَ دَعْوى الإلَهِيَّةِ، أوْ دَعْوى النُّبُوَّةِ، أوْ دَعْوى الوِلايَةِ، أوْ دَعْوى السِّحْرِ وطاعَةِ الشَّياطِينِ، فَهَذِهِ أرْبَعَةُ أقْسامٍ:
القِسْمُ الأوَّلُ: ادِّعاءُ الإلَهِيَّةِ. وجَوَّزَ أصْحابُنا ظُهُورَ خَوارِقِ العاداتِ عَلى يَدِهِ مِن غَيْرِ مُعارَضَةٍ، كَما نُقِلَ أنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ كانَ يَدَّعِي الإلَهِيَّةَ، وكانَتْ تَظْهَرُ خَوارِقُ العاداتِ عَلى يَدِهِ، وكَما نُقِلَ ذَلِكَ أيْضًا في حَقِّ الدَّجّالِ (al-Dajjal). قالَ أصْحابُنا: وإنَّما جازَ ذَلِكَ لِأنَّ شَكْلَهُ وخِلْقَتَهُ تَدُلّانِ عَلى كَذِبِهِ، فَظُهُورُ الخَوارِقِ عَلى يَدِهِ لا يُفْضِي إلى التَّلْبِيسِ.
والقِسْمُ الثّانِي: وهو ادِّعاءُ النُّبُوَّةِ، فَهَذا القِسْمُ عَلى قِسْمَيْنِ، لِأنَّهُ إمّا أنْ يَكُونَ ذَلِكَ المُدَّعِي صادِقًا أوْ كاذِبًا. فَإنْ كانَ صادِقًا وجَبَ ظُهُورُ الخَوارِقِ عَلى يَدِهِ، وهَذا مُتَّفَقٌ عَلَيْهِ بَيْنَ كُلِّ مَن أقَرَّ بِصِحَّةِ نُبُوَّةِ الأنْبِياءِ. وإنْ كانَ كاذِبًا لَمْ يَجُزْ ظُهُورُ الخَوارِقِ عَلى يَدِهِ، وبِتَقْدِيرِ أنْ تَظْهَرَ وجَبَ حُصُولُ المُعارَضَةِ.
وأمّا القِسْمُ الثّالِثُ: وهو ادِّعاءُ الوِلايَةِ، فَالقائِلُونَ بِكَراماتِ الأوْلِياءِ اخْتَلَفُوا في أنَّهُ هَلْ يَجُوزُ أنْ يَدَّعِيَ الكَراماتِ، ثُمَّ إنَّها تَحْصُلُ عَلى وفْقِ دَعْواهُ أمْ لا؟
وأمّا القِسْمُ الرّابِعُ: وهو ادِّعاءُ السِّحْرِ وطاعَةِ الشَّيْطانِ، فَعِنْدَ أصْحابِنا يَجُوزُ ظُهُورُ خَوارِقِ العاداتِ عَلى يَدِهِ، وعِنْدَ المُعْتَزِلَةِ (the Mu'tazilah) لا يَجُوزُ.
وأمّا القِسْمُ الثّانِي مِن أقْسامِ الخارِقِ: وهو أنْ تَظْهَرَ خَوارِقُ العاداتِ عَلى يَدِ إنْسانٍ مِن غَيْرِ شَيْءٍ مِنَ الدَّعاوى، فَذَلِكَ الإنْسانُ إمّا أنْ يَكُونَ صالِحًا مَرْضِيًّا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ، وإمّا أنْ يَكُونَ خَبِيثًا مُذْنِبًا.
والأوَّلُ هُوَ القَوْلُ بِكَراماتِ الأوْلِياءِ، وقَدِ اتَّفَقَ أصْحابُنا عَلى جَوازِهِ، وأنْكَرَها المُعْتَزِلَةُ إلّا أبا الحُسَيْنِ البَصْرِيَّ وصاحِبَهُ مَحْمُودًا الخَوارِزْمِيَّ.
وأمّا القِسْمُ الثّالِثُ: وهو أنْ تَظْهَرَ خَوارِقُ العاداتِ عَلى بَعْضِ مَن كانَ مَرْدُودًا عَنْ طاعَةِ اللَّهِ تَعالى، فَهَذا هُوَ المُسَمّى بِالِاسْتِدْراجِ (istidraj, gradual lead-on by God).
فَهَذا تَفْصِيلُ الكَلامِ في هاتَيْنِ المُقَدِّمَتَيْنِ. إذا عَرَفْتَ ذَلِكَ، فَنَقُولُ: الَّذِي يَدُلُّ عَلى جَوازِ كَراماتِ الأوْلِياءِ: القُرْآنُ والأخْبارُ والآثارُ والمَعْقُولُ. أمّا القُرْآنُ فَالمُعْتَمَدُ فِيهِ عِنْدَنا آياتٌ:
صفحة ٧٣
**الحُجَّةُ الأُولى:** قِصَّةُ مَرْيَمَ عَلَيْها السَّلامُ، وقَدْ شَرَحْناها في سُورَةِ آلِ عِمْرانَ فَلا نُعِيدُها.

**الحُجَّةُ الثّانِيَةُ:** قِصَّةُ أصْحابِ الكَهْفِ وبَقائِهِمْ في النَّوْمِ أحْياءً سالِمِينَ عَنِ الآفاتِ مُدَّةَ ثَلاثِمِائَةِ سَنَةٍ وتِسْعِ سِنِينَ، وأنَّهُ تَعالى كانَ يَعْصِمُهم مِن حَرِّ الشَّمْسِ، كَما قالَ: ﴿وتَحْسَبُهم أيْقاظًا وهم رُقُودٌ﴾ (الكَهْفِ: ١٨) إلى قَوْلِهِ: ﴿وتَرى الشَّمْسَ إذا طَلَعَتْ تَزاوَرُ عَنْ كَهْفِهِمْ ذاتَ اليَمِينِ﴾ (الكَهْفِ: ١٧). ومِنَ النّاسِ مَن تَمَسَّكَ في هَذِهِ المَسْألَةِ بِقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿قالَ الَّذِي عِنْدَهُ عِلْمٌ مِنَ الكِتابِ أنا آتِيكَ بِهِ قَبْلَ أنْ يَرْتَدَّ إلَيْكَ طَرْفُكَ﴾ (النَّمْلِ: ٤٠)، وقَدْ بَيَّنّا أنَّ ذَلِكَ الَّذِي كانَ عِنْدَهُ عِلْمٌ مِنَ الكِتابِ هُوَ سُلَيْمانُ، فَسَقَطَ هَذا الِاسْتِدْلالُ. أجابَ القاضِي عَنْهُ بِأنْ قالَ: لا بُدَّ مِن أنْ يَكُونَ فِيهِمْ، أوْ في ذَلِكَ الزَّمانِ، نَبِيٌّ يَصِيرُ ذَلِكَ عِلْمًا لَهُ، لِما فِيهِ مِن نَقْضِ العادَةِ كَسائِرِ المُعْجِزاتِ. قُلْنا: إنَّهُ يَسْتَحِيلُ أنْ تَكُونَ هَذِهِ الواقِعَةُ مُعْجِزَةً لِأحَدٍ مِنَ الأنْبِياءِ، لِأنَّ إقْدامَهم عَلى النَّوْمِ أمْرٌ غَيْرُ خارِقٍ لِلْعادَةِ حَتّى يُجْعَلَ ذَلِكَ مُعْجِزَةً؛ لِأنَّ النّاسَ لا يُصَدِّقُونَهُ في هَذِهِ الواقِعَةِ، لِأنَّهم لا يَعْرِفُونَ كَوْنَهم صادِقِينَ في هَذِهِ الدَّعْوى إلّا إذا بَقُوا طُولَ هَذِهِ المُدَّةِ، وعَرَفُوا أنَّ هَؤُلاءِ الَّذِينَ جاءُوا في هَذا الوَقْتِ هُمُ الَّذِينَ نامُوا قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ بِثَلاثِمِائَةِ سِنِينَ وتِسْعِ سِنِينَ. وكُلُّ هَذِهِ الشَّرائِطِ لَمْ تُوجَدْ، فامْتَنَعَ جَعْلُ هَذِهِ الواقِعَةِ مُعْجِزَةً لِأحَدٍ مِنَ الأنْبِياءِ، فَلَمْ يَبْقَ إلّا أنْ تُجْعَلَ كَرامَةً لِلْأوْلِياءِ وإحْسانًا إلَيْهِمْ.

أمّا الأخْبارُ فَكَثِيرَةٌ:

**الخَبَرُ الأوَّلُ:** ما أُخْرِجَ في «الصَّحِيحَيْنِ» (al-Sahihayn, the two Sahih collections) عَنْ أبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: أنَّ النَّبِيَّ (ﷺ) قالَ: «لَمْ يَتَكَلَّمْ في المَهْدِ إلّا ثَلاثَةٌ: عِيسى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ، وصَبِيٌّ في زَمَنِ جُرَيْجٍ النّاسِكِ، وصَبِيٌّ آخَرُ. أمّا عِيسى فَقَدْ عَرَفْتُمُوهُ، وأمّا جُرَيْجٌ فَكانَ رَجُلًا عابِدًا في بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ، وكانَتْ لَهُ أُمٌّ، فَكانَ يَوْمًا يُصَلِّي، إذِ اشْتاقَتْ إلَيْهِ أُمُّهُ، فَقالَتْ: يا جُرَيْجُ! فَقالَ: يا رَبِّ! الصَّلاةُ خَيْرٌ أمْ رُؤْيَتُها؟ ثُمَّ صَلّى، فَدَعَتْهُ ثانِيًا، فَقالَ مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ، حَتّى قالَ ثَلاثَ مَرّاتٍ، وكانَ يُصَلِّي ويَدَعُها، فاشْتَدَّ ذَلِكَ عَلى أُمِّهِ، قالَتْ: اللَّهُمَّ لا تُمِتْهُ حَتّى تُرِيَهُ المُومِساتِ. وكانَتْ زانِيَةٌ هُناكَ، فَقالَتْ لَهم: أنا أفْتِنُ جُرَيْجًا حَتّى يَزْنِيَ، فَأتَتْهُ فَلَمْ تَقْدِرْ عَلى شَيْءٍ. وكانَ هُناكَ راعٍ يَأْوِي بِاللَّيْلِ إلى أصْلِ صَوْمَعَتِهِ، فَلَمّا أعْياها راوَدَتِ الرّاعِيَ عَلى نَفْسِها، فَأتاها فَوَلَدَتْ، ثُمَّ قالَتْ: وَلَدِي هَذا مِن جُرَيْجٍ، فَأتاها بَنُو إسْرائِيلَ وكَسَرُوا صَوْمَعَتَهُ وشَتَمُوهُ، فَصَلّى ودَعا، ثُمَّ نَخَسَ الغُلامَ. قالَ أبُو هُرَيْرَةَ: كَأنِّي أنْظُرُ إلى النَّبِيِّ (ﷺ) حِينَ قالَ بِيَدِهِ: يا غُلامُ! مَن أبُوكَ؟ فَقالَ: الرّاعِي. فَنَدِمَ القَوْمُ عَلى ما كانَ مِنهم واعْتَذَرُوا إلَيْهِ، وقالُوا: نَبْنِي صَوْمَعَتَكَ مِن ذَهَبٍ أوْ فِضَّةٍ، فَأبى عَلَيْهِمْ، وبَناها كَما كانَتْ. وأمّا الصَّبِيُّ الآخَرُ، فَإنَّ امْرَأةً كانَ مَعَها صَبِيٌّ لَها تُرْضِعُهُ، إذْ مَرَّ بِها شابٌّ جَمِيلٌ ذُو شارَةٍ حَسَنَةٍ، فَقالَتْ: اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلِ ابْنِي مِثْلَ هَذا! فَقالَ الصَّبِيُّ: اللَّهُمَّ لا تَجْعَلْنِي مِثْلَهُ! ثُمَّ مَرَّتْ بِها امْرَأةٌ ذَكَرُوا أنَّها سَرَقَتْ وزَنَتْ وعُوقِبَتْ، فَقالَتْ: اللَّهُمَّ لا تَجْعَلِ ابْنِي مِثْلَ هَذِهِ! فَقالَ الصَّبِيُّ: اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْنِي مِثْلَها! فَقالَتْ لَهُ أُمُّهُ في ذَلِكَ، فَقالَ: إنَّ الشّابَّ كانَ جَبّارًا مِنَ الجَبابِرَةِ، فَكَرِهْتُ أنْ أكُونَ مِثْلَهُ، وإنَّ هَذِهِ قِيلَ: إنَّها زَنَتْ ولَمْ تَزْنِ، وقِيلَ: إنَّها سَرَقَتْ ولَمْ تَسْرِقْ، وهِيَ تَقُولُ: حَسْبِيَ اللَّهُ».

[Page 74]

The second report is the report of the cave, which is well known in the *Sihah* (the authentic collections). It comes from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Three men set out from among those before you. Night overtook them and they took shelter in a cave and entered it. A rock came down from the mountain and sealed the mouth of the cave against them. They said: 'By God, nothing will save you from this rock except that you call upon God by your best deeds.' One of them said: 'I had two elderly parents, and I would not give anyone milk to drink before them. One day I was away while they slept in the shade of a tree, and I did not leave them. I milked the milk for them as their evening drink and brought it to them, but I found them asleep. I disliked waking them, and I disliked giving milk to anyone before them. So I stood with the cup in my hand, waiting for them to awaken, until dawn broke and they woke up and drank their evening drink. O God, if I did this seeking Your face, then relieve us of what we are in, from this rock.' The rock shifted a little, but they still could not get out. Then the second said: 'I had a cousin, and she was the dearest of people to me. I sought to have her, but she refused, until a year of hardship struck her. She came to me, and I gave her a great sum of money on condition that she give herself to me. When I had power over her, she said: "You may not break the seal except by its right." So I held back from that act, left her, and left the money with her. O God, if I did this seeking Your face, then relieve us of what we are in.' The rock shifted, but still they could not get out." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Then the third said: 'O God, I hired workers and paid them all their wages except one man, who left his wage and went away. I invested his wage until it grew into much wealth. After a time he came to me and said: "O servant of God, pay me my wage." I said to him: "All that you see of your wage, the camels, the sheep and the slaves, is yours." He said: "O servant of God, are you mocking me?" I said: "I am not mocking you." So he took all of it. O God, if I did this seeking Your face, then relieve us of what we are in.' The rock moved away from the mouth of the cave, and they came out walking."

This is a sound (*hasan sahih*) hadith, agreed upon (*muttafaq ʿalayh*).

The third report is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Many a disheveled, dust-covered man with two worn garments, whom people do not esteem, would, if he swore an oath by God, have it fulfilled for him." He did not distinguish between one thing and another in what one swears by God concerning.

The fourth report: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab narrated from Abu Hurayra (may God be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ): "While a man was driving a cow on which he had loaded a burden, the cow turned to him and said: 'I was not created for this; I was created only for plowing.' The people said: 'Glory be to God! A cow speaks!' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'I believe in this, and so do Abu Bakr and ʿUmar, may God be pleased with them both.'"

The fifth report: from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "While a man was hearing a thunder or a voice in the clouds saying: 'Water the garden of so-and-so,' he went to that garden and found a man standing in it. I said to him: 'What is your name?' He said: 'So-and-so, son of so-and-so, son of so-and-so.' I said: 'What do you do with this garden of yours when you harvest it?' He said: 'Why do you ask about that?' I said: 'Because I heard a voice in the clouds saying, "Water the garden of so-and-so."' He said: 'As you have said this, I will divide it into thirds: I keep one third for myself and my family, I give one third to the poor and to the wayfarer, and I spend one third on its upkeep.'"

As for the reports (*athar*) of the marvels (*karamat*, saintly wonders) of the Rightly Guided Caliphs, we shall begin with what is related of them, and then with what appeared from the rest of the Companions.

As for Abu Bakr (may God be pleased with him), among his marvels is that when his bier was carried to the door of the tomb of the Prophet (ﷺ) and it was called out, "Peace be upon you, O Messenger of God, this is Abu Bakr at the door," the door opened, and a voice called out from the tomb: "Bring the beloved in to the beloved."

As for ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him), many kinds of his marvels appeared. One of them is what is related: he dispatched an army and appointed over them a man called Sariya ibn al-Husayn. Then one Friday ʿUmar was delivering the sermon, and while on the pulpit he began to shout in his sermon: "O Sariya, the mountain! The mountain!" ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may God honor his face, said: "I noted the date of that utterance. Then the messenger of the army arrived and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, we fought on Friday during the time of the sermon, and they defeated us. Then a man was shouting, "O Sariya, the mountain! The mountain!" So we backed our backs against the mountain, and God defeated the disbelievers, and we gained great spoils through the blessing of that voice.'" I said: "I heard some preachers say that this was a miracle of Muhammad (ﷺ), because he said to Abu Bakr and ʿUmar: 'You two are to me as the hearing and the sight.' So when ʿUmar was to Muhammad (ﷺ) as the sight, he was undoubtedly able to see from that great distance."

Second: it is related that the Nile of Egypt, in the pre-Islamic period, would stop once a year and would not flow until a single beautiful virgin was thrown into it. When Islam came, ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs wrote to ʿUmar about this event, and ʿUmar wrote on a potsherd: "O Nile, if you flow by God's command, then flow; and if you flow by your own command, then we have no need of you!" That potsherd was thrown into the Nile, and it flowed and never stopped again after that.

Third: an earthquake struck Medina, and ʿUmar struck the ground with his whip and said: "Be still, by God's leave." It became still, and the earthquake never struck Medina again after that.

Fourth: a fire broke out in some houses of Medina, and ʿUmar wrote on a potsherd: "O fire, be still by God's leave." They threw it into the fire, and it was extinguished immediately.

Fifth: it is related that an envoy of the King of the Romans came to ʿUmar and asked for his house. He assumed that his house was like the palaces of kings. They said: "He has no such house; he is in the desert, making bricks." When the envoy went to the desert, he saw ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him) with his whip placed under his head, sleeping on the dust. The envoy marveled at this and said: "The people of the East and the West fear this man, and he is in this condition!" Then he said to himself: "I have found him alone, so I will kill him and free the people from him." When he raised the sword, God brought out from the earth two lions, which attacked him. He was frightened and dropped the sword from his hand. ʿUmar awoke and saw nothing. He asked him about the situation, and he told him the event, and he embraced Islam.

I say: these incidents were transmitted through single reports (*ahad*). But there is something known by mass transmission (*tawatur*), namely that, despite his distance from the adornments of this world and his avoidance of pretense and grand displays, he governed the East and the West and overturned kingdoms and states. If you look into the books of history, you will know that nothing like what he achieved has happened to anyone from the beginning of Adam's time until now. For, despite his utter distance from pretense, how was he able to carry out those policies? There is no doubt that this is among the greatest marvels.

As for ʿUthman (may God be pleased with him), Anas related: "I was walking along the road when I raised my eyes to a woman. Then I entered upon ʿUthman, and he said: 'What is wrong with me? I see you entering upon me while the marks of fornication are visible on you!' I said: 'Has revelation come after the Messenger of God (ﷺ)?' He said: 'No, but it is a true insight (*firasa*).'"

Second: when he was struck with the sword, the first drop of his blood fell onto the *Mushaf* (the copy of the Qur'an), on the words of His exalted saying: ﴿So God will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:137).

Third: Jahjah al-Ghifari seized the staff from the hand of ʿUthman and broke it over his knee, and then a gangrene (*akala*) struck his knee.

As for ʿAli (may God honor his face), it is related that one of his lovers stole, and he was a black slave. He was brought to ʿAli, who said to him: "Did you steal?" He said: "Yes." So ʿAli cut off his hand. He left ʿAli (peace be upon him), and he met Salman al-Farisi and Ibn al-Karra. Ibn al-Karra said: "Who cut off your hand?" He said: "The Commander of the Faithful, the chief of the Muslims, the son-in-law of the Messenger, and the husband of Batul (Fatima)." He said: "He cut off your hand and you praise him?" He said: "Why should I not praise him, when he cut off my hand justly and freed me from the Fire?" Salman heard this and informed ʿAli. ʿAli called the black man, placed his hand on his forearm, covered it with a handkerchief, and made supplications. We heard a voice from heaven: "Lift the cloth from the hand!" We lifted it, and the hand had been healed by God's leave and His gracious handiwork.

As for the rest of the Companions, their conditions in this matter are many, and we mention a few of them.

First: Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir related from Safina, a freedman of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who said: "I boarded a ship, and the ship in which I was broke. I clung to one of its planks, and the plank threw me into a thicket where there was a lion. The lion came out toward me, intending to attack me. I said: 'O Abu al-Harith (the lion), I am a freedman of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), so come forward and show me the way.' Then it growled, and I thought it was bidding me farewell, and it went back."

Second: Thabit related from Anas that Usayd ibn Hudayr and another man from the Ansar were talking before the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about some matter of theirs until a portion of the night had passed. Then they left him, and the night was very dark. Each of them had a staff in his hand, and the staff of one of them lit up for them so that they walked by its light. When the path divided between them, the staff of the other lit up for him, and he walked by its light until he reached his home.

Third: they said to Khalid ibn al-Walid: "There are among your army those who drink wine." He mounted his horse one night and went around the army. He met a man on a horse with a skin of wine, and he said: "What is this?" The man said: "Vinegar." Khalid said: "O God, make it vinegar." The man went back to his companions and said: "I have brought you wine the like of which the Arabs have never drunk." When they opened it, it was vinegar. They said: "By God, you have brought us nothing but vinegar!" He said: "By God, this is the supplication of Khalid ibn al-Walid."

Fourth: the well-known incident in which Khalid ibn al-Walid ate a handful of poison in the name of God, and it did him no harm.

Fifth: it is related that Ibn ʿUmar, on one of his journeys, met a group who had halted on the road out of fear of a predatory beast. He drove the beast away from their path and then said: "A beast is only given power over the son of Adam to the extent that he fears it. If he had feared none but God, nothing would have been given power over him."

Sixth: it is related that "the Prophet (ﷺ) sent al-ʿAla ibn al-Hadrami" on a campaign, and a stretch of sea stood between them and their target. He called upon the Greatest Name of God, and they walked upon the water. In the books of the Sufis there are reports on this theme that exceed all limit and count; whoever wants them may consult them.

As for the rational proofs (*dala'il ʿaqliyya qatʿiyya*) for the permissibility of marvels (*karamat*), they are of several aspects:

The First Argument: the servant is a friend (walī) of God. God says: ﴿Indeed, the friends of God—no fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve﴾ (Yunus: 62). The Lord is the friend of the servant. God says: ﴿God is the friend of those who believe﴾ (al-Baqarah: 257). He says: ﴿And He is the friend of the righteous﴾ (al-A'raf: 196). He says: ﴿Your friend is only God and His Messenger﴾ (al-Ma'idah: 55). He says: ﴿You are our protector﴾ (al-Baqarah: 286). He says: ﴿That is because God is the protector of those who believe﴾ (Muhammad: 11). Thus it is established that the Lord is the friend of the servant, and the servant is the friend of the Lord. Also, the Lord is the beloved of the servant, and the servant is the beloved of the Lord. God says: ﴿He loves them and they love Him﴾ (al-Ma'idah: 54). He says: ﴿And those who believe are stronger in love for God﴾ (al-Baqarah: 165). He says: ﴿Indeed, God loves those who repent and loves those who purify themselves﴾ (al-Baqarah: 222).

When this is established, we say: when the servant advances in obedience to the point that he does everything God commands, and everything that pleases Him, and abandons everything God forbids and warns against, then how is it far-fetched that the Lord, the Merciful, the Generous, would grant once what the servant wishes? Rather, it is more fitting, because the servant, despite his baseness and weakness, when he did everything God wills and commands, then for the merciful Lord to grant once what the servant wishes is more fitting. For this reason God says: ﴿Fulfil My covenant, and I will fulfil your covenant﴾ (al-Baqarah: 40).

The Second Argument: if the manifestation of karama (wondrous acts of the saints) were impossible, that would be either because God is not worthy of doing such an act, or because the believer is not worthy of God giving him this gift. The first is a defect attributed to God, and it is kufr. The second is false, for knowing the essence of God, His attributes, His acts, His rulings and His names, and loving God, obeying Him, and persisting in remembrance of His holiness, glory and declaration of His oneness (tahlil), is nobler than giving a single loaf of bread in a desert, or subjugating a snake or a lion. So when He gave knowledge, love, remembrance and gratitude without any request, then for Him to give him a loaf of bread in a desert, what distance is there in that?

The Third Argument: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, relating from the Lord of Majesty: "My servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory upon him. And My servant continues to draw near to Me with voluntary acts until I love him. When I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his tongue with which he speaks, his heart with which he understands, his hand with which he strikes, and his foot with which he walks. By Me he hears, by Me he sees, by Me he speaks, and by Me he walks." This report indicates that no share remains in their hearing for other than God, nor in their sight, nor in the rest of their limbs. For if a share for other than God remained, He would not have said: "I am his hearing and his sight." Having established this, we say: there is no doubt that this station is nobler than subjugating a snake or a beast, giving a loaf of bread, a cluster of grapes, or a sip of water. So when God, by His mercy, brought His servant to these lofty ranks, what distance is there in His giving him a single loaf of bread or a sip of water in a desert?

The Fourth Argument: He (peace be upon him) said, relating from the Lord of Majesty: "Whoever shows enmity to a friend of Mine, I have declared war upon him." So He made harming the friend a substitute for harming Himself. This is close to His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you are actually pledging allegiance to God﴾ (al-Fath: 10). He also said: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when God and His Messenger have decreed a matter﴾ (al-Ahzab: 36). He also said:
[Page 77]
﴿Indeed, those who harm God and His Messenger—God has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter﴾ (al-Ahzab: 57). Thus He made the pledge to Muhammad (ﷺ) a pledge with God, the pleasure of Muhammad (ﷺ) the pleasure of God, and harming Muhammad (ﷺ) harming God. Therefore, undoubtedly, the rank of Muhammad (ﷺ) is the highest of ranks, reaching the furthest ends. Likewise here: when He said: "Whoever shows enmity to a friend of Mine, I have declared war upon him," this indicates that He made harming the friend a substitute for harming Himself. This is reinforced by the well-known report that He, may He be exalted, will say on the Day of Resurrection: "I was sick and you did not visit Me." He will say: "My Lord, how could I do that, when You are the Lord of the worlds?" He will say: "My servant so-and-so was sick, and you did not visit him. Did you not know that if you had visited him, you would have found that with Me?" The same applies to giving drink and food. These reports indicate that the friends of God reach these ranks. So what distance is there in God giving him a morsel of bread, a sip of water, or subjugating a dog or a rose for him?

The Fifth Argument: We observe in custom that when a king singles someone out for a special service and permits him to enter his council of intimacy, he may also single him out by empowering him to do what others cannot. Indeed, sound reason testifies that whenever such closeness is attained, these ranks follow it. Thus closeness is taken as the principle and rank as a consequence. The greatest of kings is the Lord of the worlds. So when He honors a servant by bringing him to the thresholds of His service and the ranks of His honor, and makes him stand upon the secrets of His knowledge, lifts the veils of distance between him and Himself, and seats him upon the carpet of His nearness, what distance is there in His manifesting some of those karamat in this world? Yet all this world, compared to an atom of those spiritual felicities and divine knowledges, is pure nothingness.

The Sixth Argument: There is no doubt that the one who directs actions is the spirit, not the body. And there is no doubt that the knowledge of God the Exalted for the spirit is like the spirit for the body, as we have established in explaining His saying: ﴿He sends down the angels with the spirit by His command﴾ (al-Nahl: 2). He (peace be upon him) also said: "I spend the night with my Lord, who feeds me and gives me drink." For this meaning, we see that whoever has more knowledge of the states of the unseen world is stronger in heart and less weak. For this reason, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God honor his face, said: "By God, I did not uproot the gate of Khaybar with physical strength, but with a divine strength." That is because 'Ali, may God honor his face, at that time, his gaze was cut off from the world of bodies, and the angels shone with the lights of the world of greatness. So his spirit became strong, took on the likeness of the noble spiritual essences, and the lights of the world of holiness and majesty shone within him. Therefore he acquired a power by which he could do what others could not. Likewise, when the servant persists in acts of obedience, he reaches the station of which God says: "I was his hearing and his sight." When that light of God's majesty becomes his hearing, he hears the near and the far. When that light becomes his sight, he sees the near and the far. When that light becomes his hand, he is able to act upon the difficult and the easy, the distant and the near.

The Seventh Argument: This is based on rational and philosophical principles. We have shown that the essence of the spirit is not of the kind of perishable, corruptible bodies that are subject to dispersal and disintegration. Rather, it is of the kind of the essences of the angels, the inhabitants of the heavens, and the type of the holy and purified beings. However, when it attached itself to this body and became absorbed in managing it, it became so absorbed that it forgot its first homeland and its original dwelling, and became entirely like this corruptible body. Its strength weakened, its capacity departed, and it was no longer able to do any of the actions. But when it becomes familiar with the knowledge and love of God, its absorption in managing this body decreases, the lights of the sacred celestial throne-spirits shine upon it, and from those lights it is overflowed. Then it becomes strong enough to act upon the bodies of this world, like the strength of the celestial spirits over these works. That is the karamat. There is also another subtle point: our doctrine is that human spirits differ in their essence. Some are strong and some weak, some luminous and some turbid, some free and some base. The celestial spirits are likewise. Do you not see how God described Gabriel: ﴿Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger, possessing power, with rank before the Lord of the Throne, obeyed and trustworthy﴾ (al-Takwir: 19–21). And He said of another group of angels: ﴿And how many an angel there is in the heavens whose intercession will avail nothing﴾ (al-Najm: 26). So it is likewise here. When a soul has the holy, elemental power, its essence radiant and its nature lofty, and then there are added to it the kinds of spiritual exercises that remove from its face the dust of the world of generation and corruption, it shines, glitters, and becomes strong enough to act upon the matter of the world of generation and corruption, by the aid of the light of knowledge of the eternal presence, and by strengthening the lights of the presence of majesty and might. Let us here draw the reins of exposition, for beyond it are subtle secrets and profound states; whoever has not reached them does not believe in them. We ask God for help in attaining the good.

* * *

Those who deny the karamat argued with several points:

The First Doubt, which is the one they rely upon and by which they mislead: the appearance of something extraordinary that breaks habit was made by God a proof of prophethood. So if it occurred for a non-prophet, this proof would be invalidated, because the presence of a proof without what it proves undermines its being a proof. And this is false.

The Second Doubt: they held to the words of the Prophet (peace be upon him), relating from God, glorified be He: "Those who draw near to Me will never draw near with anything like the performance of what I have made obligatory upon them." They said: this indicates that drawing near to God through performing obligatory duties is greater than drawing near to Him through performing voluntary acts. Then, one who draws near to Him through obligatory duties does not receive any karamat. So one who draws near through voluntary acts is even more deserving of not receiving them.

The Third Doubt: they held to His saying: ﴿And it carries your loads to a land you could not reach except with great difficulty to yourselves﴾ (al-Nahl: 7). They said: the claim that the friend travels from one land to a distant land, not in the usual manner, contradicts this verse. Also, Muhammad (ﷺ) did not reach Medina from Mecca except over many days with severe hardship. How, then, can it be conceived that the friend travels from his own land to the Hajj in a single day?

The Fourth Doubt: they said: if this friend, who manifests karamat, claims a dirham from a person, shall we demand evidence from him or not? If we demand evidence from him, it would be pointless, because the appearance of karamat upon him indicates that he does not lie, and in the presence of a decisive proof, how can a conjectural proof be demanded? And if we do not demand it from him, then we have abandoned his saying (peace be upon him): "The evidence is upon the claimant." This indicates that the claim of karama is false.

The Fifth Doubt: if the karama is permissible for some of the friends, it is permissible for the rest. So if karamat multiply until they break habit, they will proceed in accordance with habit, and that undermines both the miracle (mu'jiza) and the karama.

The response to the first objection: scholars have disagreed over whether a wali (a friend of God, a saint) may claim walayah (sainthood). Some of the muhaqqiqun (the verifying scholars, the careful theologians) said that this is not permissible. On this view the difference between mu'jizat (prophetic miracles) and karamat (saintly marvels) is that a miracle is preceded by a claim to prophethood, while a karamah is never preceded by a claim to walayah. The reason for this difference is that the prophets, peace be upon them, were sent to mankind so that they might become callers from unbelief to faith and from disobedience to obedience. If the claim to prophethood were not made, the people would not believe in them, and if they did not believe, they would remain in unbelief. When the prophets claim prophethood and show a miracle, the people believe in them. So the prophets' undertaking to claim prophethood is not aimed at exalting themselves, but at showing compassion to creation, so that people may move from unbelief to faith. As for the wali's walayah, ignorance of it is not unbelief, nor is knowing it faith. Therefore a claim to walayah would be a pursuit of the desire of the self. We thus know that the prophet must openly claim prophethood, while the wali may not claim walayah, and the difference becomes clear.

[Page 79]

As for those who said that a wali may claim walayah, they mentioned the differences between miracle and karamah in several respects:

First: the appearance of an act that breaks the customary order indicates that this person is free from sin. Then, if this act is accompanied by a claim to prophethood, it indicates that he is truthful in his claim to prophethood, and if it is accompanied by a claim to walayah, it indicates that he is truthful in his claim to walayah. By this means, the appearance of karamat among the awliya' is not a challenge to the miracles of the prophets, peace be upon them.

Second: the prophet (ﷺ) claims a miracle and affirms it with certainty, whereas the wali, if he claims a karamah, does not affirm it with certainty, because a miracle must be manifest, while as for a karamah, its manifestation is not obligatory.

Third: it is obligatory to negate opposition (mu'aradah) from a miracle, but it is not obligatory to negate it from a karamah.

Fourth: we do not permit the appearance of a karamah upon the wali when he claims walayah unless he acknowledges, at the time of that claim, that he is upon the religion of that prophet. When this is the case, that karamah becomes a miracle of that prophet and a confirmation of his message. On this assumption, the appearance of a karamah does not discredit the prophethood of the prophet, but rather strengthens it.

The answer to the second objection: drawing near to God through the obligatory acts alone is more perfect than drawing near through the supererogatory acts. As for the wali, he is a wali only if he performs both the obligatory and the supererogatory acts, and there is no doubt that his state is more complete than the state of one who restricts himself to the obligatory acts. Thus the difference becomes clear.

The answer to the third objection: the saying of God, exalted is He, ﴿And He carries your loads to a land you could not have reached except with great hardship to yourselves﴾ is to be understood in its known and customary sense, whereas the karamat of the awliya' are rare states, and so they are like exceptions to that general rule. This is the answer to the fourth objection, namely the reliance on the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: "The burden of proof lies on the one who claims."

The answer to the fifth objection: the obedient ones among them are few, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And few of My servants are grateful﴾ (Saba': 13), and as Iblis said: ﴿and You will not find most of them grateful﴾ (al-A'raf: 17). When few are obedient, the karamat that appear upon them in rare times do not discredit the fact that they are outside the customary order.

* * *

The seventh issue: on the difference between karamat and istidraj (a gradual, deceptive granting of what one wants). Know that whoever wills something and God gives him what he wills does not thereby show that this servant is esteemed before God, Exalted, whether the gift is in accordance with custom or not. Rather, it may be an honour for the servant, and it may be istidraj for him. This istidraj has many names in the Qur'an:

The first: istidraj. God, Exalted, said: ﴿We will draw them gradually from where they do not know﴾ (al-Qalam: 44). The meaning of istidraj is that God gives him everything he wants in this world, so that his error, his misguidance, his ignorance and his obstinacy increase, and he grows further from God each day. Its verification: it has been established in the rational sciences that repetition of acts is a cause for the acquisition of a firm disposition. When the heart of the servant inclines toward this world and then God gives him what he wants, the seeker then reaches the sought object, and this produces pleasure; pleasure increases inclination, and inclination produces greater effort. Each of these two states continues to lead to the other, and each of these two states grows stronger degree by degree. It is known that occupation with these hastening pleasures prevents one from the stations of unveiling and the degrees of knowledge, so inevitably his distance from God increases degree by degree until it is complete. This is istidraj.

The second: makr (cunning, plotting). God, Exalted, said: ﴿So none feels secure from the plot of God except the losing people﴾ (al-A'raf: 99); ﴿They plotted, and God plotted, and God is the best of plotters﴾ (Al 'Imran: 54); and He said: ﴿They plotted a plot, and We plotted a plot, while they did not perceive﴾ (al-Naml: 50).

The third: kayd (scheming). God, Exalted, said: ﴿They deceive God, but He is the one who deceives them﴾ (al-Nisa': 142), and He said: ﴿They think to deceive God and those who believe, but they deceive only themselves﴾ (al-Baqarah: 9).

The fourth: imla' (respite, granting time). God, Exalted, said: ﴿Let not those who disbelieve think that Our giving them respite is good for them; We only give them respite that they may increase in sin﴾ (Al 'Imran: 178).

The fifth: ihlak (destruction). God, Exalted, said: ﴿until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly﴾ (al-An'am: 44), and He said concerning Pharaoh: ﴿And he and his soldiers were arrogant in the land without right, and they thought that they would not be returned to Us﴾, ﴿So We seized him and his soldiers and threw them into the sea﴾ (al-Qasas: 39–40). It becomes clear from these verses that reaching what one desires does not indicate the attainment of high degrees or the winning of good things. It remains for us to mention the difference between karamat and istidraj. We say: the possessor of a karamah does not take comfort in that karamah. Rather, when a karamah appears, his fear of God, Exalted, becomes greater and his caution against the subjugation of God becomes stronger, for he fears that it may be from the category of istidraj. But the possessor of istidraj takes comfort in what appears upon him, and he thinks that he has only obtained that karamah because he deserved it. At that point he despises others and becomes arrogant toward them, and he feels secure from the plot and punishment of God and does not fear a bad end. So when any of these states appear upon the possessor of what seems to be a karamah, this indicates that it was istidraj and not a karamah. For this reason the muhaqqiqun said: most of what happens of separation from the presence of God occurs in the station of karamat. Therefore you will find the muhaqqiqun fearing karamat just as they fear various kinds of trial. What shows that taking comfort in a karamah cuts one off from the path is the following:

The first proof: this delusion arises only when a man believes that he deserves this karamah, for if he were not deserving of it, rejoicing in it would be impossible. Rather, his joy at the generosity and grace of the Master should be greater than his joy in himself. Thus it is established that joy in the karamah is greater than joy in oneself, and it is established that joy in the karamah does not occur except when one believes himself to be worthy and deserving of it. This is pure ignorance, for the angels said: ﴿We have no knowledge except what You have taught us﴾ (al-Baqarah: 32), and God, Exalted, said: ﴿They did not measure God with His true measure﴾ (al-An'am: 91). Moreover, it has been established by certain proof that no creature has any right upon the Truth, so how can the thought of deserving arise?

The second proof: karamat are things distinct from the Truth, may He be glorified. Joy in the karamah is joy in other than the Truth, and joy in other than the Truth is a veil from the Truth, and how can joy and delight befit one who is veiled from the Truth?

The third proof: whoever believes of himself that he has become deserving of the karamah because of his deed, his deed takes on great weight in his heart, and whoever has weight given to his deed is ignorant. Had he known his Lord, he would know that all the obedience of creatures is deficient in the face of God's majesty, that all their thanks are insufficient in the face of His bounties and blessings, and that all their knowledge and sciences are bewilderment and ignorance in the face of His might. I saw in some books that a reciter recited in the assembly of the master Abu 'Ali al-Daqqaq the saying of God, Exalted: ﴿To Him ascends the good word, and the righteous deed raises it﴾ (Fatir: 10). He said: the sign that the Truth has raised your deed is that it does not leave its remembrance in your sight. If your deed remains in your view, it is rejected, and if it does not remain with you, it is raised and accepted.

The fourth proof: the possessor of a karamah was given the karamah only to display humility and lowliness in the presence of God. If he exalts himself, becomes domineering and arrogant because of these karamat, then this path of his acquisition leads him to its loss, and so it is rejected. For this reason, when the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned his own virtues and merits, he would say at the end of each one of them: "wa la fakhr" (and I do not boast), meaning: I do not boast of these karamat; I boast only of the Bestower and the Giver.

The fifth proof: the apparent karamat granted to Iblis and to Bal'am were great, and then it was said to Iblis: ﴿and he was among the disbelievers﴾ (al-Baqarah: 34), and it was said of Bal'am: ﴿his likeness is that of a dog﴾ (al-A'raf: 176). And it was said of the learned men of the Children of Israel: ﴿The likeness of those who were entrusted with the Torah and then did not carry it is like that of a donkey carrying books﴾ (al-Jumu'ah: 5). And it was also said of them: ﴿And those who were given the Book did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves﴾ (Al 'Imran: 19). Thus He made clear that their falling into darkness and misguidance was caused by their rejoicing in what they had been given of knowledge and asceticism.

The sixth proof: the karamah is other than the one who is honoured, and whatever is other than the one who is honoured is contemptible, and whoever takes might through the contemptible is contemptible. For this reason the Friend (Khalil), may God's blessings be upon him, said: "As for You, no." Seeking self-sufficiency through the poor is poverty, strengthening oneself through the weak is weakness, completing oneself through the deficient is deficiency, rejoicing in the created is folly, and wholly turning to the Truth is deliverance. Thus it is established that the poor man, if he rejoices in the karamah, falls from his rank. But if he witnesses in the karamat only the One who honours, and in the honour only the One who grants honour, and in creation only the Creator, then arrival is then worthy.

The seventh proof: self-glorification and taking pride in one's attributes are among the attributes of Iblis and Pharaoh. Iblis said: ﴿I am better than him﴾ (al-A'raf: 12), and Pharaoh said: ﴿Is not the dominion of Egypt mine?﴾ (al-Zukhruf: 51). Whoever falsely claims divinity or prophethood has no aim except to adorn the self and strengthen greed and self-admiration. For this reason he (peace be upon him) said: "Three things destroy," and he concluded with the words: "and a man's self-admiration."

The eighth proof: God, Exalted, said: ﴿So take what I have given you and be among the grateful﴾ (al-A'raf: 144), and ﴿And worship your Lord until certainty comes to you﴾ (al-Hijr: 99). When God gave him the great gift, He commanded him to occupy himself with serving the Giver, not with rejoicing in the gift.

Argument Nine: When God gave the Prophet (ﷺ) the choice between being a king-prophet and being a servant-prophet, he left kingship. There is no doubt that possessing a kingdom that spans the East and the West is among the noble marvels (karamat), indeed among the miracles. Yet he (ﷺ) left that kingship and chose servanthood, because if one is a servant, his pride is in his Master, and if one is a king, his pride is in his subjects. So when he chose servanthood, he inevitably made the sunnah in the tashahhud (the sitting recitation in prayer) narrated by Ibn Mas'ud: "I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His messenger." And at the Mi'raj (the Night Ascension) it was said: ﴿Glory be to Him who took His servant by night﴾ (al-Isra: 1).

Argument Ten: The lover of the Master is one thing, and the lover of what belongs to the Master is another. Whoever loves the Master does not rejoice in anything other than the Master, and does not find intimacy in anything other than the Master. Finding intimacy in other than the Master and rejoicing in other than Him shows that he was not a lover of the Master, but a lover of his own self's share, and the share of the self is sought only for the self. This person therefore loved only himself. The Master was not beloved to him; rather he made the Master a means to attain that sought object. The greatest idol is the self, as God the Exalted said: ﴿Have you seen him who takes his own desire as his god?﴾ (al-Jathiya: 23). This person is therefore a worshipper of the greatest idol. To the point that the verifiers (muhaqqiqun) said: there is no harm in worshipping any of the idols comparable to the harm in worshipping the self, and there is no fear from worshipping idols comparable to the fear of rejoicing in marvels.

Argument Eleven: God the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever fears God, He will make for him a way out﴾ ﴿and will provide for him from where he does not expect. And whoever relies upon God, then He is sufficient for him﴾. This indicates that whoever does not fear God and does not rely upon Him, nothing from these actions and states will be attained for him.

[p. 82]

Question Eight: Does the walī (friend of God) know that he is a walī? Ustadh (teacher) Abu Bakr ibn Furak said: it is not permissible. Ustadh Abu Ali al-Daqqaq and his student Abu al-Qasim al-Qushayri said: it is permissible. The arguments of those who prevent it are several:

First argument: If a man knew that he was a walī, security (al-amn) would be attained for him, by the evidence of God's saying: ﴿Indeed, the friends of God—no fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve﴾ (Yunus: 62). But attaining security is impermissible, and several things indicate this:

One: God's saying: ﴿So none feels secure from the plan of God except the losing people﴾ (al-A'raf: 99). Despair is also impermissible, due to God's saying: ﴿Indeed, none despairs of relief from God except the disbelieving people﴾ (Yusuf: 87), and His saying: ﴿And who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except the astray?﴾ (al-Hijr: 56). The meaning is that security is attained only through belief in God's incapacity, and despair is attained only through belief in His stinginess. Belief in incapacity or stinginess regarding God is disbelief. Therefore attaining security and despair are both disbelief.

Two: Although obedience may be abundant, the subjugating power of the Truth is greater, and while that subjugation is dominant, security is not attained.

Three: Security requires the removal of servanthood and the abandonment of service, and the abandonment of servanthood entails enmity. Security also requires the abandonment of fear.

Four: God described the sincere ones by saying: ﴿And they call upon Us in hope and in fear, and they were humbled before Us﴾ (al-Anbiya: 90). It was said: "in hope of Our reward and fear of Our punishment." It was said: "in hope of Our bounty and fear of Our justice." It was said: "in hope of Our union and fear of Our separation." The best view is to say: "in hope in Us, and fear of Us."

Second argument (that the walī does not know he is a walī): The walī becomes a walī only because the Truth loves him, not because he loves the Truth. The same applies to the enemy. Then, the love of the Truth and its enmity are two secrets that no one perceives. So the obedience and disobedience of servants do not affect the love of the Truth or its enmity, because obedience and disobedience are originated, whereas God's attributes are eternal and infinite, and the originated finite does not come to dominate the eternal infinite. On this basis, a servant may at the present moment be in the very act of disobedience, yet his portion from eternity is pure love. And a servant may at the present moment be in the very act of obedience, yet his portion from eternity is pure enmity. The complete verification is this: His love and enmity are an attribute, and an attribute of the Truth is not caused by a reason. Whoever is loved without cause cannot become an enemy because of the cause of disobedience, and whoever is hated without cause cannot become a lover because of the cause of obedience. Since the love of the Truth and its enmity are two secrets that cannot be perceived, Jesus, peace be upon him, said: ﴿You know what is in my self, and I do not know what is in Yours. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen﴾ (al-Ma'ida: 116).

Third argument: The judgment that a person is a walī, and that he is among the people of reward and Paradise, depends on the end (al-khatima). The evidence is God's saying: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times its like﴾ (al-An'am: 160). He did not say "whoever does a good deed." This indicates that the entitlement to reward is derived from the end, not from the beginning of the deed. What confirms this is that if a person spent his life in disbelief and then embraced Islam at the end, he is among the people of reward, and the reverse is also true. This is evidence that the criterion is the end, not the beginning of the deed. For this reason God said: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: if they desist, what has already passed will be forgiven for them﴾ (al-Anfal: 38). Thus it is established that the criterion for wilaya, for enmity, and for whether one is among the people of reward or the people of punishment, is the end. It becomes clear that the end is known to no one. Therefore it is necessary to affirm with certainty that the walī does not know that he is a walī.

As for those who said that the walī may know that he is a walī, they argued for the soundness of their view that wilaya has two pillars:

One: that he is outwardly submissive to the Shari'a (the sacred law).

Two: that inwardly he is absorbed in the light of reality (haqiqa). When both matters are present and the person knows that they are present, he inevitably knows that he is a walī. As for outward submission to the Shari'a, it is evident. As for the inner absorption in the light of reality, it is that his joy is in obeying God, his intimacy is in the remembrance of God, and he has no settling with anything other than God.

The answer: The admixture of errors in this domain is great and obscure, and judgment is difficult. Experimentation is dangerous, and certainty is delusion. Between a person and arrival at the realm of lordship (rububiyya) lie veils, sometimes of fires and other times of lights. And God knows the realities of secrets.

[p. 83]

Let us return to the exegesis (tafsir).

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 18, verses 13–15:

God, exalted is He, says: ﴿We relate to you their story with truth. Indeed, they were youths who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance﴾ ﴿and We strengthened their hearts when they stood up and said: "Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth; we will never invoke any god besides Him. We would have then uttered an outrageous excess (shatat)"﴾ ﴿"These people of ours have taken gods besides Him. Why do they not bring a clear authority (sultan bayyin) concerning them? Who then is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against God?"﴾.

Know that God, exalted is He, first mentioned a summary of their account, then said: ﴿We relate to you their story with truth﴾, meaning in accordance with truthfulness. ﴿Indeed, they were youths who believed in their Lord﴾: they were a group of young men who believed in God. Then God, exalted is He, said concerning their attributes: ﴿and We strengthened their hearts﴾, meaning We inspired them with patience and made them firm. ﴿When they stood up﴾. Regarding this standing up, there are several opinions:

The first: Mujahid said: They were the great men of their city. They went out and gathered outside the city without a prior appointment. A man among them, the eldest of the people, said: "I find in myself something that I do not think anyone else finds." They said: "What do you find?" He said: "I find in myself that my Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth."

The second opinion: They stood before their king, the tyrant Diqyanus (Decius), and said: "Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth." This was because he was calling people to worship the idols (tawaghit). So God made these youths firm and protected them until they disobeyed that tyrant, acknowledged the lordship of God, and openly declared their disavowal of partners and rivals.

The third opinion, which is the view of Ata and Muqatil, is that they said this when they rose from sleep. This is far-fetched, because God resumed their story with His words: ﴿We relate to you﴾ and His words: ﴿We would have then uttered an outrageous excess﴾. The meaning of shatat in the language is exceeding the limit. Al-Farra' said: It is said "qad ashatta fi al-sawm" when one exceeds the limit in bargaining, and only ashatta yushittu ishtatan and shatatan has been heard. Al-Zajjaj and others report that shatta al-rajul and ashatta mean when a man exceeds the limit. From this is His saying: ﴿and do not exceed (tushtit)﴾ (Sad: 22). The origin of this is from the saying: "shattat al-dar" when the house became distant. So shatat is distance from the truth. Here it is in the accusative as a verbal noun (masdar), and the meaning is: "We would have then uttered a statement of excess."

As for His saying: ﴿These people of ours have taken gods besides Him﴾, this is from the speech of the Companions of the Cave, and they mean those who were in the time of Diqyanus who worshipped idols. ﴿Why do they not bring a clear authority concerning them?﴾ (lawla ya'tuna, meaning halla ya'tuna: "why do they not bring") ﴿concerning them﴾, i.e., concerning the worship of the gods, ﴿with a clear proof﴾.

[Page 84]

The meaning of ﴿concerning them﴾ is concerning the worship of the gods. The meaning of the speech is that the absence of a clear proof, through the lack of indications for that, does not indicate the non-existence of what is signified. Some people argue from the absence of evidence to the absence of what is evidenced, and they infer the soundness of this method from this verse, saying: God, exalted is He, inferred the non-existence of partners and rivals from the absence of evidence for them, so it is established that inferring the non-existence of the signified from the absence of evidence is a strong method. Then He said: ﴿Who then is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against God?﴾, meaning that to judge that a thing is established while there is no evidence for it is injustice and fabrication against God and a lie about Him. This is among the greatest proofs of the corruption of the view based on taqlid (blind imitation).

The commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on Surah 18, verses 16–17:

The Lord's word: ﴿And when you withdraw from them and what they worship, except Allah, then take refuge in the cave; your Lord will spread out for you of His mercy and will prepare for you a means of ease in your affair.﴾ ﴿And you would see the sun, when it rises, inclining away from their cave to the right, and when it sets, passing them on the left, while they are in a wide space within it. That is among the signs of Allah. Whomever Allah guides is the one guided, and whomever He leaves astray, you will not find for him a guiding ally.﴾

Know that the meaning is that some of them said to others: ﴿And when you withdraw from them﴾, meaning you withdraw from what they worship, except Allah. So you have not withdrawn from the worship of Allah. ﴿Then take refuge in the cave.﴾ Al-Farra' said: this is the answer (jawab) to "idh" (when), as you say, "When you did such-and-such, then do such-and-such." Its meaning is: go to it and make it your refuge. ﴿Your Lord will spread out for you of His mercy﴾, meaning He will extend it over you. ﴿And will prepare for you a means of ease in your affair (mirfaqan).﴾ Nafi', Ibn 'Amir and 'Asim, in one narration, read mirfaqan with a fatha on the mim and a kasra on the fa'. The rest read mirfaqan with a kasra on the mim and a fatha on the fa'. Al-Farra' said: both are dialects, and their derivation is from irtifaq (gaining benefit). Al-Kisa'i used to reject, for the elbow of a person (which is in the hand), anything other than a kasra on the mim and a fatha on the fa', while al-Farra' permitted it both for affair and for the hand. It was also said: both are dialects, but the fatha is more analogical (qiyas) and the kasra is more common. It was also said: al-mirfaq is that by which one benefits, and al-marfiq with a fatha is the act of benefiting. Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And you would see the sun, when it rises, inclining away from their cave to the right, and when it sets, passing them on the left.﴾ On this there are several discussions:

The first discussion: Ibn 'Amir read tazwarru with a sukun on the unpointed za' and a shadda on the ra', like tahmarru. 'Asim, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read tazawaru with an alif and without shadda. The rest read tazzawaru with a shadda and an alif. All have one meaning. Al-tazawur is inclination and deviation. From it comes zarahu, when he inclined toward him. Al-zur is deviation from truth. As for the shadda, its origin is tatazawaru, the second ta' was made sukun and assimilated (idgham, merging of one letter into another) into the za'. As for the lightened form, it is tafa'ala from al-zawr. As for tazwarru, it is from al-izwirar (turning away).

The second discussion: His words ﴿And you would see the sun﴾ mean that you, the addressee, see the sun at its rising inclining away from their cave. It is not meant that the one addressed sees this meaning, but the custom of address is in this manner. Its meaning is that if you had seen it in this form.

The third discussion: His words ﴿to the right (dhat al-yamin)﴾ mean the direction of the right. Its origin is that dhat is an adjective placed in the position of the noun modified, because it is the feminine of dhu in their saying: a man dhu mal (possessor of wealth), and a woman dhat mal. The sense is as if it were said: it inclines away from their cave in the direction of the right (dhat al-yamin).

As for His words ﴿and when it sets, passing them on the left (taqridu-hum dhat al-shimal)﴾, there are two discussions:

The first discussion: Al-Kisa'i said: qaradtu al-makan means I turned away from it. Abu 'Ubayda said: qard is in several things, among them cutting, and likewise travelling through lands, meaning when one crosses them. You say to your companion, "Did you pass by such-and-such a place?" and the answerer says, "I only crossed it." So His words ﴿passing them on the left﴾ mean it deviates from the direction of their heads toward the direction of the left.

The second discussion: The commentators have two views here.

The first view: The door of that cave was open to the north side. When the sun rose, it was on the right of the cave, and when it set, it was on its left. So the light of the sun did not reach inside the cave, but good air and suitable breeze did reach it. The purpose is that Allah, exalted is He, protected the People of the Cave from the sunlight falling upon them, for otherwise their bodies would have decayed. Thus they were preserved from putrefaction and corruption.

The second view: The intended meaning is not that. Rather, the meaning is that when the sun rose, Allah prevented the light of the sun from reaching them, and likewise when it set. This was a act beyond custom (fi'l khariq lil-'adah) and a great karamah (wonder granted to saints), with which Allah specially favoured the People of the Cave. This is the view of al-Zajjaj, who argued for its soundness with His words ﴿That is among the signs of Allah.﴾ He said: If the matter were as the people of the first view stated, it would be a customary and familiar matter, and it would not be among the signs of Allah. But if we take the verse in this second sense, it would be a wondrous karamah, and so it would be among the signs of Allah. Know that He, exalted is He, then informed that they were in a spacious part of the cave where the cold of the wind and the breeze of the air reached them. He said: ﴿while they are in a wide space within it﴾, meaning within the cave. Al-fajwa is an open space in a place. Abu 'Ubayda said: its plural is fajawat. From it is the hadith: "When he found a fajwa, he hastened (nassa)."

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿That is among the signs of Allah.﴾ On this there are two views:

Those who said that it prevents the light of the sun from reaching them by His power said: the intended meaning of "that" is that inclining and deviation. Those who did not say this said: the intended meaning of "that" is that protection which Allah granted them in that cave for that long period, among the signs of Allah that point to the wonders of His power and the marvels of His wisdom. Then He, exalted is He, explained that just as their remaining for that long period, preserved from death and destruction, was among His arrangements, His gentleness and His generosity, so too their initial turning away from disbelief and their desire for faith was by Allah's help and gentleness. So He said: ﴿Whomever Allah guides is the one guided﴾, like the People of the Cave. ﴿And whomever He leaves astray, you will not find for him a guiding ally﴾, like Decianus the disbeliever and his companions. The debates of the people of compulsion (al-jabr) and free will (al-qadar) regarding this verse are well known.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 18, verse 18:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And you would think them awake, while they are asleep. And We turn them to the right and to the left, and their dog stretches out its forelegs at the threshold. If you had looked upon them, you would have turned away from them in flight and been filled with terror of them.﴾

Know that the meaning of His saying ﴿and you would think them﴾, according to what we mentioned in His saying ﴿and you see the sun﴾, is: if you had seen them, you would have thought them ﴿awake﴾. It is the plural of yaqiz and yaqzan (awake). This was said by al-Akhfash, Abu 'Ubayda and al-Zajjaj, and they cited Ru'ba's verse:

"And they found their brothers awake"

Similar to it is the saying: najd, nujdan and anjad (plural forms). ﴿And they are asleep﴾ means they are sleeping. It is a verbal noun (masdar) used in the sense of the passive participle (ism al-maf'ul), as one says "qawmun ruku' wa qu'ud wa sujud," describing a plural with a verbal noun. As for the one who said it is the plural of raqid, he has erred, because fa'il is not pluralized as fu'ul. Al-Wahidi said: they are thought to be ﴿awake﴾ because their eyes are open while they are asleep. Al-Zajjaj said: because of their great turning, it is supposed that they are awake. The evidence for this is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We turn them to the right and to the left.﴾

They differed regarding the duration of the turning. From Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, it is related that they had two turnings each year. From Mujahid: they remain on their right sides for nine years, then they are turned onto their left sides, and they remain asleep for nine years. It was also said: they had one turning on the day of 'Ashura'. I say: the sense cannot reach these estimates, the wording of the Qur'an does not indicate them, and if a sound report had come concerning them, how could it be known? Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: the purpose of turning them is so that the earth does not consume their flesh and does not decay them.

I say: this is strange, because He, Exalted is He, who was able to keep their lives for three hundred years and more, why would He not be able to preserve their bodies as well without turning?

His saying ﴿dhat﴾ is in the accusative as an adverb of place, because the meaning is ﴿and We turn them﴾ in the direction of ﴿the right﴾, or on the side of ﴿the right﴾, as we said in His saying: ﴿inclining away from their cave to the right (dhat al-yamin)﴾. As for His saying ﴿and their dog stretches out its forelegs﴾, Ibn 'Abbas and most of the commentators said: they fled by night from their king, and they passed by a shepherd who had a dog, and it followed them in their religion, along with its dog. Ka'b said: they passed by a dog, which barked at them, and they drove it away, but it returned, and they did this several times. The dog said to them: "What do you want from me? Do not fear my side; I love the beloved ones of Allah, so sleep, and I will guard you." 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr said: that was their hunting dog. The meaning of ﴿stretching out its forelegs﴾ is that it lays them upon the ground spread out, not folded. From this is the hadith concerning prayer: "He forbade spreading out the forelegs like a beast of prey (iftirash al-sab')," and he said: "Do not spread your forelegs like a beast of prey (iftirash al-sab')." As for His saying ﴿at the threshold (bi-l-wasid)﴾, it means the courtyard of the cave. Al-Zajjaj said: al-wasid is the courtyard of a house and the courtyard of a dwelling, and its plurals are wasa'id and wusud. Yunus, al-Akhfash and al-Farra' said: al-wasid and al-asid are two dialectal forms, like al-wikaf and al-ikaf. Al-Suddi said: ﴿al-wasid﴾ is the doorway, and the cave does not have a door or a threshold, but he meant that the dog was at the place of the threshold of the house.

Then He said: ﴿If you had looked upon them﴾, i.e., had you come upon them, one says: "ittala'tu 'alayhim," meaning "I came upon them," and one says: "at-la'tu fulanan 'ala al-shay'," meaning "I made someone aware of the thing, so he became aware." His saying ﴿you would have turned away from them in flight (firaran)﴾: al-Zajjaj said: ﴿firaran﴾ is in the accusative as a verbal noun, because the meaning of "wallaytu minhum" is "farartu." ﴿And you would have been filled with terror of them (ru'ban)﴾, i.e., fear and dread. It was said in the exegesis: their hair and nails grew long, and their eyes remained open while they slept; for this reason, whoever saw them would flee from them in terror. It was also said: He, Exalted is He, placed them in such a state that whoever saw them was seized with severe fear. As for the detailed cause of the terror, Allah knows it best, and this is the more correct view.

His saying ﴿and you would have been filled with terror of them﴾: Nafi' and Ibn Kathir read "lamul-lit" with a doubled lam and hamza, while the rest read it with a single lam. It is also related from Ibn Kathir that he read it with a single lam. The meaning is the same, except that doubling conveys emphasis. Al-Akhfash said: the single form is more elegant in Arabic speech; one says "mala'tanee ru'ban" (you filled me with terror), and they scarcely recognize "mallatanee." This is supported by the more common usage, such as the verse: "fa-yamla'u baytana aqitan wa samnan" (so it fills our house with curds and butter), and another's saying: "wa min mali'in 'aynayhi min shay'in ghayrihi idha raha najwa al-jamrati al-bidi ka-l-duma" and another's: "la tamla' al-dalwa wa 'araqun fiha" and another's: "imtala'a al-hawdu wa qala qatni." Doubled usage also occurs, and they cited al-Mukhabbal al-Sa'di: "wa idha qatala al-Nu'man bi-l-nasi muhriman fa-mullia min 'Awf ibn Ka'b salasiluhu."

Ibn 'Amir and al-Kisa'i read ru'ban with a damma on the 'ayn throughout the Qur'an, while the rest read it with sukun.

The statement of Him, exalted is He: ﴿And thus We raised them up, that they might question one another.﴾ ﴿A speaker among them said, "How long have you remained?" They said, "We have remained a day or part of a day." They said, "Your Lord knows best how long you have remained. So send one of you with this silver of yours to the city, and let him see which of them has the purest food, and bring you provision from it. Let him be discreet and let him not make anyone aware of you."﴾ ﴿For if they gain power over you, they will stone you or return you to their religion, and then you will never prosper.﴾

The implied meaning is: "Just as We increased them in guidance, bound their hearts, struck their ears so that they slept, kept them alive without eating or drinking, and turned them over..., thus We raised them, that is, We revived them from that sleep which resembles death, ﴿that they might question one another﴾ as a questioning of dispute and disagreement about the length of their stay." If it is asked: Could the purpose of raising them be that they question and dispute with one another? We say: That is not far-fetched, for when they questioned one another, there were revealed to them wondrous matters of God's power and strange conditions, and that revelation is desired in itself.

Then He said: ﴿A speaker among them said, "How long have you remained?"﴾ That is, what is the measure of our stay in this cave? ﴿They said, "We have remained a day or part of a day."﴾ The exegetes said: They entered the cave in the morning, and God raised them at the end of the day; therefore they said, "We have remained a day." Then, when they saw the sun still up, they said, "Or part of a day."

Then He said: ﴿They said, "Your Lord knows best how long you have remained."﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: this was their leader, Yamlikha, who referred the knowledge of that to God, because when he looked at their hair, their nails, and the skin of their faces, he saw in them signs of severe change, and so he knew that such change does not occur except over long days.

[Page 88]

Then he said: ﴿So send one of you with this silver of yours to the city.﴾ Abu ʿAmr, Hamza, and Abu Bakr, on the authority of ʿAsim, read بِوَرْقِكم (biwarqikum) with the *raʾ* silent and the *waw* fatha. Others read it with the *waw* kasra and the *raʾ* silent. Ibn Kathir read بِوَرِقِكم (biwariqikum) with the *raʾ* kasra and the assimilation (idgham) of the *qaf* into the *kaf*. Ibn Muhaysin is reported to have kasra'd the *waw* and silenced the *raʾ* and assimilated the *qaf* into the *kaf*, but this is not permissible, because of the meeting of two silent letters (iltiqa' al-sakinayn) in this form. The word waraq is a name for silver, whether minted or not, and this is supported by the report that ʿArfajah made a nose from waraq. It has dialectal variants: wariq, warq, and wirq, like kabid, kabd, and kibd. This was mentioned by al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj. Al-Farra' said: the kasra of the *waw* is the weakest of them. It is also said that waraq is called ar-riqqah. Al-Azhari said: its origin is wariq, like silah and ʿidah.

The exegetes said: They had with them dirhams bearing the image of the king who ruled in their time. By "the city" is meant the one called today Tarsus.

This verse indicates that striving to secure provisions is an important and lawful matter, and that it does not nullify reliance on God (tawakkul).

As for His words: ﴿Let him see which of them has the purest food.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: he means what is lawful of the slaughtered animals, because most of the people of their land were Magians, and among them were people who concealed their faith. Mujahid said: their king was a tyrant, so their words ﴿purest food﴾ mean: which of them is furthest from usurpation (ghasb). It is also said: which is the best and most delicious; and it is said: which is the cheapest. Al-Zajjaj said: the phrase أيُّها (ayyuha, "which of them") is in the nominative as the subject of the inchoative (ibtida'), أزْكى (azka, "purest") is its predicate, and طَعامًا (taʿaman, "food") is in the accusative as a specification (tamyiz).

As for His words: ﴿And let him be discreet﴾ (wal-yatalattaf), that is, let that be done in secrecy and concealment, namely entering the city and buying the food. ﴿And let him not make anyone aware of you﴾, that is, let him not inform anyone of the people of the city of your whereabouts.

﴿For if they gain power over you﴾, that is, if they come upon and overlook your place or yourselves. It comes from their saying: "I gained power over so-and-so" when you rise above him, and "I gained power over the roof" when you stand upon it. From this is His saying: ﴿So they became uppermost﴾ (al-Saff: 14), that is, dominant. Likewise His saying: ﴿that He may make it prevail over all religion﴾ (al-Tawbah: 33), that is, that He may exalt it.

As for His words: ﴿they will stone you﴾, that is, they will kill you. Stoning (rajm) in the sense of killing is frequent in the revelation (tanzil), as in His saying: ﴿Had it not been for your tribe, we would have stoned you﴾ (Hud: 91), and His saying: ﴿that you stone me﴾ (al-Dukhan: 20). Its origin is throwing. Al-Zajjaj said: that is, they will kill you by stoning, and stoning is the most vile kind of killing.

﴿Or they will return you to their religion﴾, that is, they will bring you back to their faith. ﴿And then you will never prosper﴾, that is, if you return to their faith, you will never be successful in this world or in the Hereafter. Al-Zajjaj said: His words ﴿then never﴾ indicate a condition, meaning: and you will never prosper if you return to their creed.

Al-Qadi said: What is more grievous for a believer who flees with his religion than these two? In one of them is destruction of the self, namely stoning, which is the most vile kind of killing, and in the other is destruction of the religion, by being returned to disbelief.

If it is asked: Is it not the case that if they were compelled to disbelieve, so that they outwardly displayed disbelief, no harm would come upon them? So how did they say: ﴿and then you will never prosper﴾? We say: It is possible that what is meant is that if they returned these Muslims to disbelief by way of compulsion, they would remain outwardly displaying that disbelief for a period, and their hearts would incline to that disbelief, and they would become disbelievers in reality. So this possibility exists, and that was what they feared from it. And God knows best.
